summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change removes the only authorization check on `DELETE /users/<user>`, turning a privileged destructive operation into an open endpoint.

## Analysis

`delete_user` previously required `@require_role("admin")`. The PR replaces that guard with a comment so cleanup jobs running as `viewer` stop getting 403s. That fixes the symptom by deleting the access control entirely: any caller who can reach the route can remove any user from `USERS` and receive `204`.

The failure mode is immediate and concrete. With the decorator gone there is no role check, no caller identity check, and no substitute gate (service account, internal-only middleware, signed job token, etc.). A viewer session, an unauthenticated client, or any scripted caller can delete `alice` or `bob`.

If cleanup jobs need delete access, grant that capability narrowly (dedicated job role/credential, server-side job path, or an allowlisted principal) while keeping human/interactive callers on least privilege. Removing `@require_role` is not an acceptable fix for job 403s.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The base revision guarded DELETE /users/<user> with @require_role("admin"); head replaces that decorator with a comment and leaves delete_user with no auth check, so any client can remove users and get 204. That is a real access-control regression on a destructive route.
